title: Putin welcomes Trump’s peace envoys but has no intention of ending the war
gist: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited both Moscow and Kyiv for the first time, but produced no meaningful progress: Putin told them Russia is making 'real progress' on the battlefield and stressed addressing the 'root causes' of the conflict. Zelenskyy now acknowledges the war is likely to continue into 2027 and is seeking Patriot interceptors and additional US LNG for the winter, while the author argues Putin's maximalist aims — demilitarization and 'denazification' meaning the end of Ukrainian statehood — are incompatible with any negotiated settlement.

insights.claim: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited both Moscow and Kyiv on the same tour for the first time, but despite upbeat assessments from all participants there was no sign the meetings produced meaningful progress toward peace.
insights.so_what: Discount upbeat diplomatic readouts as a signal; the absence of substantive outcomes despite the symbolic first is the informative fact.
insights.locator: United States envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: The proposals Witkoff and Kushner presented are thought to include deescalation measures to limit attacks on energy infrastructure and grain shipments, which Zelenskyy called 'actually very good, very worthy.'
insights.so_what: An energy-and-grain-only deescalation deal is the most tradeable near-term outcome and would directly affect refined product, crude, and wheat risk premia.
insights.locator: The Ukrainian leader commented that some of the proposals
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Kremlin foreign policy adviser Yuri Ushakov said Putin told the US envoys that Russia was making real progress on the battlefield and was confident of achieving its military objectives while stressing the necessity of addressing all the root causes of the conflict.
insights.so_what: The readout is the clearest available evidence that Moscow has not moderated its terms — negotiations are a stalling instrument, not a convergence process.
insights.quote: all the root causes of the conflict
insights.locator: Speaking after the meeting, Kremlin foreign policy adviser
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

themes.theme: Kyiv is planning for a longer war

insights.claim: Following talks with the US envoys, Zelenskyy acknowledged that the war is likely to continue into 2027.
insights.so_what: The Ukrainian president's own base case extends past 2026 — a concrete anchor for defense procurement, energy, and commodity risk horizons.
insights.quote: he acknowledged that the war is likely to continue into 2027
insights.locator: At the same time, Zelenskyy appears to be under no illusions
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Zelenskyy's winter wish list is interceptor missiles for Ukraine's Patriot air defense systems and increased energy supplies, with Kyiv hoping to secure additional LNG deliveries from the United States.
insights.so_what: Ukrainian LNG demand from the US is an incremental structural buyer for American cargoes into a tight European winter market.
insights.locator: The Ukrainian President’s winter wish list
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Zelenskyy is pushing for a second envoy visit and stressed the importance of not having long pauses, noting the Americans had been to Moscow many times but Kyiv only once.
insights.so_what: The asymmetry in visit counts is Kyiv's implicit complaint about mediation balance — a tell about how the process is weighted.
insights.quote: They have been to Moscow many times, and this was the first time in Kyiv
insights.locator: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has repeatedly invited
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Russia's objectives in Ukraine extend far beyond the limited territorial demands at the heart of current negotiations, aiming to reassert Russian dominance over Ukraine and erase the notion of a separate Ukrainian national identity.
insights.so_what: If territory is not the objective, territorial concessions cannot buy peace — the core reason to assign low probability to any land-for-peace settlement.
insights.locator: This emphasis on the “root causes of the conflict”
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Russia's bid to demilitarize Ukraine has backfired disastrously, with Ukraine emerging since 2022 as the strongest fighting force in Europe and a world leader in drone warfare, yet the Kremlin still insists any peace deal must impose extensive restrictions on Ukraine's military.
insights.so_what: Ukraine's drone-warfare leadership is a durable European defense-industrial asset created by the war — relevant to NATO procurement and defense-tech investment.
insights.quote: with the country emerging since 2022 as the strongest fighting force in Europe and a world leader in drone warfare
insights.locator: So far, Russia’s bid to demilitarize Ukraine has backfired
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: The 'denazification' of Ukraine has come to be understood as the complete eradication of Ukrainian sovereignty and national identity, with Kremlin media using frequent genocidal language and confirming that denazification means de-Ukrainization.
insights.so_what: Defines the war aim as existential rather than territorial, which sets the ceiling on what any mediator can deliver.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: A Kremlin memorandum produced ahead of the summer 2025 Istanbul talks spelled out Russia's terms: sweeping territorial concessions, military restrictions, a ban on international alliances, official status for the Russian language, reinstated privileges for the Russian Orthodox Church, a Kremlin-friendly version of Ukrainian history, and a ban on all so-called nationalist Ukrainian political parties.
insights.so_what: A documented, itemized maximalist list is the concrete evidence against the view that Moscow's demands are negotiable at the margin.
insights.locator: In summer 2025, Russia’s vision for addressing
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Banning all so-called nationalist Ukrainian political parties would pave the way for installing a pro-Russian puppet regime, reversing decades of nation-building and ending Ukrainian statehood even if the Kremlin maintained a charade of sovereignty.
insights.so_what: Names the specific mechanism — party bans, not annexation — by which a signed peace deal could still end Ukrainian independence.
insights.locator: Crucially, all so-called “nationalist” Ukrainian political parties
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Trump's envoys continue to discuss win-win scenarios whereas Putin is playing a zero sum game, a mismatch in negotiating frameworks that dooms the current diplomatic approach.
insights.so_what: A framework mismatch, not a bargaining gap, is the diagnosis — meaning more meetings will not converge and mediation optimism should be faded.
insights.quote: Trump’s envoys continue to discuss win-win scenarios, whereas Putin is playing a zero sum game.
insights.locator: Trump’s envoys continue to discuss win-win scenarios
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Putin's invasion of Ukraine is not a land grab or a geopolitical real estate deal but an attempt to reverse the Soviet collapse and revive the Russian Empire, and peace will only be possible when diplomatic efforts reflect that reality.
insights.so_what: The imperial-restoration frame implies the war risk extends beyond Ukraine to the wider post-Soviet space — a reason to price durable European defense spending.
insights.quote: It is an attempt to reverse the Soviet collapse and revive the Russian Empire.
insights.locator: His invasion of Ukraine is not a land grab
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Putin's uncompromising stance in the Kremlin talks should serve as a wake-up call for anyone still in doubt about the extent of his imperial ambitions or his refusal to accept the post-1991 emergence of an independent Ukraine, though it does not make further negotiations futile.
insights.so_what: The author keeps a door open for diplomacy while ruling out near-term settlement — the realistic base case is continued war with episodic talks.
insights.locator: Putin’s uncompromising stance during Saturday’s Kremlin talks
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
